title: Fraud alert queue, June to September 2026

findings.headline: Nearly 9 in 10 alerts are false positives
findings.detail: Only 313 of 3,000 alerts (10.4%) were confirmed fraud, so most analyst time goes on genuine customers. The confirmed rate is flat by month: 10.5% in June, 9.7% in September.

findings.headline: Three rules produce most of the confirmed fraud
findings.detail: Mule account inbound confirms at 31.7% (243 alerts), New device + high amount at 21.9% (556) and Velocity at 15.4% (408). Round-amount transfer (0.6%) and Night-time login (1.6%) confirm very rarely across 997 alerts combined.

findings.headline: New device + high amount hit rate is climbing
findings.detail: Its confirmed rate rose from 18.1% in June to 24.3% in September. This is worth checking now, as it is one of the largest rules at 18.5% of alerts.

findings.headline: Larger amounts go with higher fraud rates
findings.detail: The top fifth of alerts by amount (above 34,533) confirms at 19.8%, against 3.7% in the lowest fifth (up to 7,344). Handling time shows a similar pattern, with 33.3% confirmed in the slowest fifth (over 15 minutes).

findings.headline: Analyst confirmed rates vary, but the mix may explain it
findings.detail: Among the eight analysts shown, rates range from 6.0% (Analyst 06) to 13.1% (Analyst 05), a 7.1-point spread. Rule mix and amounts may differ by analyst, so this is not yet a performance judgement.

next_steps: Review whether Round-amount transfer and Night-time login rules can be tightened or de-prioritised, as they confirm at 0.6% and 1.6%.
Investigate why New device + high amount confirmed rates rose from 18.1% to 24.3%, and whether alert thresholds should change.
Compare analyst confirmed rates after adjusting for rule mix, and check the four analysts not shown in the summary.

reviews.note: Numbers match (313 of 3,000; 10.4%; 10.5% to 9.7%). Removed the claim about analyst time and genuine customers, which the summary does not show.
Rates and counts match. 997 = 512 + 485. The three rules hold about 262 of 313 confirmed (243×31.7%, 556×21.9%, 408×15.4%), so 'most' holds.
18.1% to 24.3% rises each month, but it covers four months only. Lowered severity to medium. It is the second-largest rule, not the largest.
Amount figures match, though the rise is not smooth (8.5%, 7.5% in the middle). Slowest fifth is 15 minutes or more. Handling time follows the outcome, not the reverse.
6.0% and 13.1% are right, but the 7.1-point spread covers only eight shown analysts. Reworded as no performance conclusion; chance may play a part.

findings.headline: Nearly 9 in 10 alerts are false positives
findings.detail: Only 313 of 3,000 alerts (10.4%) were confirmed fraud, so 89.6% were false positives. The monthly confirmed rate stays between 9.7% and 11.1%, with no clear trend.

findings.headline: Three rules produce most of the confirmed fraud
findings.detail: Mule account inbound confirms at 31.7% (243 alerts), New device + high amount at 21.9% (556) and Velocity at 15.4% (408). Round-amount transfer (0.6%) and Night-time login (1.6%) confirm rarely across 997 alerts combined.

findings.headline: New device + high amount confirmed rate rose each month
findings.detail: Its confirmed rate went 18.1%, 22.1%, 23.6%, 24.3% from June to September. It is 18.5% of all alerts, so the trend is worth watching.

findings.headline: Larger amounts go with higher confirmed fraud rates
findings.detail: The top fifth of alerts by amount (above 34,533) confirms at 19.8%, against 3.7% in the lowest fifth (up to 7,344). Alerts taking 15 minutes or more confirm at 33.3%, but longer handling probably follows a likely fraud case.

findings.headline: Analyst confirmed rates differ among the eight shown
findings.detail: Among the eight analysts shown, rates run from 6.0% (Analyst 06) to 13.1% (Analyst 05). The other four are not shown, and rule mix may differ by analyst, so this is not a performance judgement.

next_steps: Review the Round-amount transfer and Night-time login rules (0.6% and 1.6% confirmed), first checking what real fraud they catch before tightening them.
Find out why the New device + high amount confirmed rate rose from 18.1% to 24.3%, and whether it needs more analyst capacity.
Compare analyst confirmed rates within each rule, and get figures for all 12 analysts before drawing any conclusion.
conclusion: The queue is mostly false positives (89.6%), and the confirmed rate depends heavily on the rule, from 0.6% to 31.7%. Fraud is concentrated in Mule account inbound, New device + high amount and Velocity. First, review the two lowest-yield rules, Round-amount transfer and Night-time login, after checking what fraud they do catch.
limits: This review uses one summary of one four-month extract, so it cannot show why rates differ, how much fraud the rules miss, or what a false alert costs.
